title: Telemetry: burst admission/denial metrics + pool saturation gauges (cardinality-safe)
author: Logan Wright
release_notes: Emit burst admission/denial metrics with deny reason codes (cardinality-safe).
Add per-pool saturation gauges and capacity signal plumbing for dashboards/alerts.
Add per-tenant burst usage counters behind sampling + allowlist to avoid high-cardinality blowups.
body:
Context: Dedicated Burst adds a controlled shared burst pool. For pilot/GA we need (a) clear admission vs denial visibility, (b) saturation/health signals per burst pool, and (c) per-tenant attribution hooks without blowing up Prometheus/TSDB cardinality. This PR implements burst telemetry primitives in the data plane + metrics library and wires them through the routing context.

What’s in this PR: Adds metrics for burst admission flow: redwood_burst_admission_total{result,deny_reason,region,pool,gpu_class} and redwood_burst_admission_latency_ms buckets keyed only on low-cardinality dimensions; deny_reason is a bounded enum (not freeform). Adds pool saturation gauges sourced from fleet signals: redwood_burst_pool_tokens_per_second_utilization (0..1), redwood_burst_pool_concurrency_utilization (0..1), and redwood_burst_pool_capacity_state{state} as a 0/1 gauge with a bounded state set (ok|degraded|saturated|unknown). Adds per-tenant burst usage counters (requests/tokens) but gates tenant_id labeling behind: (1) an explicit allowlist of pilot tenants, (2) 1/N sampling for non-allowlisted tenants, and (3) a hard cap on distinct tenant series per process (LRU drop with log warning). For all tenants we still emit aggregate usage without tenant_id. Also adds structured log fields and trace attributes for full-fidelity forensics: burst.requested, burst.admitted, burst.pool, burst.deny_reason, burst.limit_class, burst.policy_cache_hit.

Cardinality controls (important): We do NOT emit model_name or route_name on burst admission counters (too many series). We do NOT emit raw tenant_id by default; only allowlisted + sampled. deny_reason is a closed set defined in code. pool is a stable short name (e.g., "us-east-1/h100/shared-burst-a") and gpu_class is bounded. Region is bounded. Any unexpected values are mapped to "unknown" and we increment redwood_burst_metric_sanitization_total{metric,field} to make sanitization visible.

Why now: ENG-4826 is a dependency for dashboards/alerts work (ENG-4827) and for pilot shadow metering validation (ENG-4830). This also unblocks SRE to define saturation alerts and correlate p99 drift with pool utilization.

Testing: Unit tests for label sanitization + deny_reason mapping. Integration test in telemetry harness to ensure series cap is enforced and that allowlist overrides sampling. Load test validation run in staging: verified <3k additional active series per region when allowlist is empty; with 3 pilot tenants allowlisted we stayed within budget and got per-tenant visibility.

Rollout notes: Metrics are behind feature flag telemetry.burst_metrics_enabled (default off). When enabled, per-tenant metrics additionally require telemetry.burst_tenant_metrics_enabled and a non-empty allowlist. Safe to enable in prod progressively (one region at a time).
commits: telemetry: define burst metrics + deny reason enum
telemetry: add label sanitization + bounded mapping utilities
routing: propagate burst context into metrics scope + structured logs
fleet signals: wire pool utilization gauges into telemetry emitter
config: add flags for burst metrics + tenant allowlist
conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we avoid adding model_name to any of these? It will explode series. Also, what’s the plan for tenant visibility for support cases?

Logan Wright (author): Agreed—no model_name/route_name labels in this PR. For tenant visibility we rely on: (1) allowlist for pilot tenants, (2) sampling for non-allowlisted, and (3) trace attributes + structured logs for full-fidelity. Added explicit notes + a sanitization counter to detect unexpected label values.
Nadia Rahman (review): For deny_reason, please ensure it’s a closed enum and never uses raw policy strings. Also, can we separate "denied_due_to_cooldown" vs "denied_due_to_pool_saturated"?

Logan Wright (author): Updated: deny_reason is now a bounded enum in code, mapping from policy decision codes. Added separate values: cooldown, pool_saturated, tenant_cap, region_ineligible, global_circuit_breaker, unknown. No raw strings in labels.
Peter Holtz (review): SRE ask: we need to be able to alert on admission failures that are due to our systems vs customer-config caps. Can we add a higher-level result class?
Logan Wright (author): Added limit_class label with bounded values (customer|platform|unknown) on the admission_total metric only. This stays low-cardinality and should help alert tuning.
Sergio Costa (review): Please document the recommended dashboard queries (admit rate, top deny reasons, pool utilization). Also ensure the metric names follow our conventions.
Logan Wright (author): Added docs/internal/telemetry/burst-metrics.md with example PromQL and naming rationale. Renamed pool gauges to include "utilization" suffix to match convention.
Allison Grant (approval): Looks good with the gating + caps. Approving contingent on default flags staying off.
Logan Wright (author): Confirmed defaults are off in defaults.yaml; staging enables only the aggregate metrics for validation.
